question: From 2013 to 2025, did the risk of a motorist being killed for each mile driven in NYC go down? Use this crash data to make a chart and answer the question.

options.metric: Annual number of motorists killed in police-reported crashes
options.reason: Annual fatalities directly show the overall motorist death burden, even though they do not adjust for how much driving occurred.
options.answer: Annual motorist fatalities fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 (26% lower), but this crash file cannot tell whether deaths per mile driven fell because it has no vehicle-miles-traveled data.
options.interpretation: This framing answers whether the annual number of motorists killed was lower at the end of the period: the count fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, with a peak of 139 in 2020. It is a defensible measure of the death burden recorded in crashes, but it leaves the per-mile risk question unanswered because driving exposure is not measured.

options.denominator: All police-reported crashes in that year
options.reason: Normalizing deaths by reported crashes gives a crash-based severity measure that adjusts for the number of reported crashes each year.
options.answer: Motorist fatalities per 100,000 reported crashes rose from 54.0 in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025 (about 75% higher), but this is not a per-mile rate and cannot establish whether per-mile risk fell.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how the number of motorist deaths compares with the volume of reported crashes: the ratio was higher in 2025 than 2013 and surged in 2020. It is a defensible crash-based severity indicator, but it leaves risk per mile unanswered because crashes are not a measure of miles driven.

answer:
Annual motorist fatalities fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 (26% lower), but this crash data cannot establish whether deaths per mile driven fell because it has no vehicle-miles-traveled data.  
Motorist fatalities per 100,000 reported crashes rose from 54.0 in 2013 to 94.7 in 2025 (about 75% higher), but this is not a per-mile rate and cannot establish whether per-mile risk fell.
